title: Investigation of vegetative, neurological, and genetic parameters in the context of bimaxillary repositioning osteotomy in patients with chronic obstructive sleep apnea (OSAS) – a prospective, monocentric study
summary:
This study investigates autonomic, neurological, and genetic parameters in patients with chronic obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) who undergo bimaxillary osteotomy or maxillomandibular advancement (MMA). This surgical therapy is used particularly when patients do not tolerate continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) breathing and has high success rates.

The aim of the study is to assess changes in various physical, hormonal, cognitive, and genetic parameters before and four months after surgery.

Main hypothesis:

Four months after surgery, there will be a significant improvement in the apnea/hypopnea index (AHI) compared to the preoperative baseline.

Secondary hypotheses:
Postoperative changes are expected with regard to:
Quality of life (ESS, Berlin Questionnaire, STOP-BANG)
Stress levels and the hormonal stress axis (e.g., cortisol, prolactin, testosterone)
Hunger and satiety parameters (e.g., glucose, insulin, IGF-1)
Cognitive function and brain activity (fMRI)
Inflammatory markers and immunological parameters (e.g., IL-6, hsCRP, TNFα)
Vital parameters (blood pressure, heart rate, HRV, BMI, etc.)
Gene expression of circadian rhythms compared to pre-operative and a control group
Primary endpoint: Improvement in AHI.

Secondary endpoints: Improvement in quality of life, stress hormones, metabolic and cognitive parameters, circadian gene expression, and vital and inflammatory markers.

Since obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a significant widespread disease with a prevalence of approximately 6%, and many affected individuals do not tolerate mask therapy, this study aims to improve our understanding of the disease and its associated physiological processes. The results are intended to contribute to the further development of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Individuals ≥ 18 years of age

Patients with severe chronic obstructive sleep apnea for whom surgical intervention is indicated.

- Surgical intervention with anterior advancement of the upper and lower jaw with additional counter-clockwise rotation
- Capacity to consent
- Signed informed consent form
Inclusion criteria for controls:

- Individuals ≥ 18 years of age
- No chronic obstructive sleep apnea
- Capacity to consent
- Signed informed consent form

Behavioral guidelines for Expression Clock genes:

- No shift work or jet lag within the previous week

Examinations
- Women in the study were not menstruating at the time of sample collection
- Breakfast between 7:00 and 8:00 a.m., lunch between 11:30 a.m. and 1:30 p.m., dinner between 5:30 and 7:30 p.m.

- Bedtime before midnight
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 years
- Missing informed consent
- Individuals incapable of giving consent/under legal guardianship
- Regarding clock genes: Pre-existing conditions: psychiatric disorders, hypersomnia,

insomnia, medications affecting sleep (e.g., melatonin or benzodiazepines), pre-existing malignant conditions

(These pre-existing conditions affect circadian rhythms and thus the expression of clock genes)
